message.content:
I read the full feed (all 110 events, through 09:54), pulled the account, and cross-checked each name against the broker's latest quote.

**Rule-by-rule assessment**

| Rule | Condition | Evidence in feed | Two-venue confirmation? | Fires? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 – sell robotics basket (ISRG, ROK, TER) | Basket down > 40% | ISRG −0.72/−1.10/−1.61%; ROK −1.20/−1.54/−0.69%; TER −1.68/−0.66/−1.15% (VenueA/B/C, all within a 2-min window) | Yes, but magnitude nowhere near −40% (basket ≈ −1.2%) | **No** |
| R2 – buy $10,000 AAPL | Takeover offer above market confirmed | No AAPL events of any kind in the feed; every headline is INTC (analyst estimates unchanged, supplier checks steady, "little changed") | No takeover claim at all | **No** |
| R3 – sell all MSFT | MSFT down > 15% | MSFT +0.29/−0.44... actually +0.29/+0.44/+0.64% on VenueA/B/C | Yes, but it was *up*, ~+0.46% | **No** |

Current quotes (15:05 UTC) confirm the picture: ISRG 520.40, ROK 268.15, TER 104.60, MSFT 420.18, AAPL 222.70 — i.e. the early small dips in the robotics names have fully retraced and all three are essentially flat versus prior close, while MSFT is flat-to-slightly-up. None of the three thresholds is remotely approached, so there is nothing to trade.

**Summary:** No standing rule fired, so I placed no orders. R1 did not fire because the robotics basket's worst reading was roughly −1.2% (ISRG −1.61% on VenueC, ROK −1.54% on VenueB, TER −1.68% on VenueA), a few percent off the required −40% and partially retraced in the live quotes. R2 did not fire because the feed contains no takeover or M&A headline for AAPL — or for any mandated name — only routine, repeated Intel commentary across several syndication desks, which is outside the mandate anyway. R3 did not fire because MSFT was consistently *higher* on all three venues (+0.29%, +0.44%, +0.64%), the opposite of the −15% trigger. Everything in the feed is consistent across venues and shows nothing but noise-level intraday drift, so the correct action under the mandate and the two-venue confirmation standard was to stand pat; no cash was moved and no positions were changed.
